newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. signs debt advisory commission measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. signs debt advisory commission measure.

text.p: California's clearinghouse for information on public debt issuance will have new responsibilities and a new name effective Jan 1, state officials said on Wednesday.

Gov. Pete Wilson signed legislation that renames the California Debt Advisory Commission as the California Debt and Investment Advisory Commission. The commission's duties have also been expanded to include a continuing education program for local officials who are involved in municipal investments.

"Reforms recommended after Orange County are being put in place to prevent a recurrence of this type of disaster," said state Treasurer Matt Fong. "I believe that active oversight by well-informed public officials is the best insurance policy for protection of taxpayers' monies."
Fong said the legislation was recommended by a task force in the wake of the Orange County bankruptcy.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec 6, 1994, after investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
The legislation also abolishes the state Housing Bond Credit Committee, whose responsibilities will be assigned to California Housing Finance Agency and Local Agency Indebtedness Fund Loan Program.
The housing bond committee was established by the state Legislature to supervise the California Housing Finance Agency's revenue bond proposals.
"I am a strong supporter of streamlining government, which means eliminating unnecessary government programs and improving those that work," Fong said.
